general_information.Description: This course focuses on fundamental conceptual and practical dimensions of intercultural communication in everyday life in social interactions in multicultural environments. It aims at developing an individual’s intellectual appreciation for cultural differences and sensitivity regarding intercultural interactions. Course objectives: 1. Discuss basic concepts, conceptual frameworks, and some broader contexts of cross culture communication; 2. Analyze and discuss examples of cross-cultural conflicts in a variety of situations; 3. Develop an understanding of barriers to effective intercultural communication; 4. Develop intercultural sensitivity in terms of beliefs, values, and norms; 5. Develop an understanding of intercultural competence.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Understand the relationship between Communication and Culture and their elements;
Recognize the Deep Structure of Culture: Lessons from the Family;
Understand Cultural History of different countries/ religions;
Understand the Cultural Explanations of Life and Death; concepts related religions and some popular religions in the world;
Identify Cultural Values and apply some Guidelines for Behavior
Understand the concepts and relationship between culture and identity;
Deepy understand and apply verbal language in communication;
Deepy understand and apply non-verbal language in communication;
Understand Cultural Influences on different Communication Contexts including business, education and health care context; the challenges of intercultural comminucation.

assessments.Question Type: Each student chooses one sub-topic related to the contents covered in the course and write about it. The assignment is supposed to be 1000-1500 words long.

assessments.Note: Participation grade will be given based on students' preparation, quantity as well as quality of participation in classroom; quality of participation is demonstrated through asking relevant questions, making statements that add to and facilitate class discussion, and builds upon others’ comments.

assessments.Duration: 30' (20 mins to present and 10 mins for Q & A)
assessments.Question Type: The whole class is divided into groups. Each group is assigned to choose one topic related to the contents covered in the textbook and present about it in 20 minutes, 10 mins for Q & A.
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Based on topics of studied units (Suggestions: greeting custom, wedding customs, social etiquete, Issues of Belonging, guesture interpretation, etc)
assessments.Note: The mark will be given based on each student's performance, not on the whole group's. It means each student will get his own mark.
